newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares jump on renewed foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares jump on renewed foreign buying.

text.p: Slovenian shares jumped 3.89 percent on Wednesday, pushed up by increased foreign buying interest, and traders said gains may well continue until the end of the month.

"Foreign investors are definitely ready to come back, especially by investing in pharmaceutical and food processing industries," Florian Hellmich, equity analyst at Vienna-based Investmentbank Austria said.
The 10-share SBI index rose 45.9 points to 1,227.3, the highest since October 21.
"Our opinion of the Slovenian market's short-term future is quite positive and I expect shares to keep rising over the next month," Hellmich added.
Davor Dubokovic, of Eastbrokers cited both the expected listing of pharmaceutical company Krka in Slovenia and of SKB bank abroad as "positive movements" the market recently.
The bank in November announced plans to list its shares on London Stock exchange and is now waiting for the necessary licence from Slovenia's central bank.

"Beside that extensive buyings by foreigners and the possibility that Drnovsek could be elected for the new Prime Minister are also factors making atmosphere more optimistic, at least in the short term," Dubokovic added.
Slovenia's centre-left acting prime minister Janez Drnovsek on Wednesday appeared likely to win a parliamentary vote to form the next government after a rightwing deputy defected from his party.
Turnover rose to 234.0 million tolars from 141.9 million tolars. Overall nine shares rose, five fell and 10 were untraded.
Bank SKB was the most actively traded share, firming 2.80 percent to 44,000 tolars on volume of 2,894 shares for total turnover of 127.9 million tolars.
"Prices of SKB's shares may exceed 60,000 tolars once it is listed abroad," one trader said.
Brokerage Dadas led the day's gainers, jumping 14.52 percent to 7,100 tolars on volume of 314 shares.
Traders said Dadas rose in reaction to recent steep falls and that only dealers interested in short-term gains were dealing with Dadas.
Trading company Kovinotehna led the day's decliners, falling 7.93 percent to 395 tolars on volume of 495 shares. -- Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
